issue.title: Race condition in assigning callbacklist handle
issue.body:
There could be a race condition in assigning handle [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/3131cc9b34b04d6d7affb09d3ad2fdbf81c677af/src/mavsdk/core/callback_list_impl.h#L23) can do something like _last_id.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);

Another thing i noticed is nested subscriptions wouldn't work from callbacks. Maybe we should add a comment for it, or better do deferred subscriptions as well like removals.

comments.body:
Hmm. What if we extend the mutex around that part?

Would nested subscriptions work using `std::recursive_mutex` and would that be safe?

I didn't wanna use a recursive mutex (hard to debug), and extending the mutex to cover the handle got a bit complicated(with deferred subs), so I went with atomic which works, and seems to be the kind of thing it is designed for. I also added deferred subscriptions, you can see it [here](https://gist.github.com/devbharat/ce952fc9f32a9771c7be1c2a62fc31a0).

I also created something similar to the MavlinkMessageHandler class that uses a map of msgid to callbacklists, but crucially it allows adding subscriptions from within callbacks (if you get this mavlink message, send this message and are now interested in this mavlink message kind of workflow), which meant (in addiiton to deferred subs in cblist) the execution of the callbacklist from MavlinkMessageHandler needed to be outside the lock (comparison [here](https://gist.github.com/devbharat/17a11229bd7df818f9a7fd65828f4ddd)). Not sure if it is generally interesting for everyone.
I like the deferred subscription and removal! It would be great if you can make a pull request for it.
@devbharat I think this would still be great :)

issue.title: Add conditional callback, use atomic handle_id and add some tests

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Fixes https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2215

Adds
 - Conditional callbacks for one-shot callback where you want unsubscription to happen automatically without dealing with the Handle object
 - Atomic _last_id to make sure when subscribing in burst from many threads at once each id is unique
 - Deferred subscriptions so you can also add subscriptions within the callback
 - Some tests

I needed to add these to create something similar to the MavlinkMessageHandler class that uses a map of msgid to callbacklists, but crucially it allows adding subscriptions from within callbacks (if you get this mavlink message, send this message and subscribe to this mavlink message kind of chained workflow), which meant (in addiiton to deferred subs in cblist) the execution of the callbacklist from MavlinkMessageHandler needed to be outside the lock (comparison [here](https://gist.github.com/devbharat/17a11229bd7df818f9a7fd65828f4ddd)).
